title: Cerulean AI - Endpoint-level Cost & Telemetry Console Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE gave a Console walkthrough focused on endpoint/route-level telemetry and per-endpoint cost attribution. Cerulean is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated for a public customer-facing API; key concerns: chargeback to product teams, latency SLOs for low-latency serving, and audit/compliance (SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: send pricing tiers, security pack, run a weekday throughput benchmark, and schedule a deep technical session for VPC/private deployment architecture.
topics: overview of per-endpoint telemetry and attribution
route/endpoint cost breakdown and chargeback examples
Dedicated vs Hosted routing and fallback policies
security/compliance: SSO, SOC2, KMS, audit logs
next_steps: Maya to send detailed pricing tiers and example chargeback spreadsheet by 2026-08-07
Darren to share security pack + SOC2 and SAML docs by 2026-08-06
Cerulean to provide 3 representative endpoints and traffic traces for bench by 2026-08-12
Schedule VPC/deployment deep dive with Infra (Marcus) week of 2026-08-17

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 16:00 PT | Duration 46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Darren O'Neil (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Cerulean Head of Platform), Marcus Hale (Cerulean Infra Eng), Priya Kapoor (Cerulean FinOps)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and Darren our systems lead is here to walk through the Console telemetry and endpoint-level cost attribution. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Doing well, thanks. We are excited, we want to see how Redwood can give us per-endpoint visibility — we run a handful of public endpoints and need to charge back to product owners.
[00:16] Marcus Hale: Quick note — we care about P99 latency under 250ms for the search endpoint, and the generative summarization can be a bit more lenient. Also, security: SAML SSO and KMS are non-negotiable.
[00:25] Priya Kapoor: And finance wants predictable cost allocation. We need per-endpoint granularity for internal billing — ideally broken down by model variant and token class.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Great, that's exactly what we'll show. Darren, want to kick off with the Console?
[00:37] Darren O'Neil: Yep. Sharing screen now — give me a sec. (short pause) Alright, you should see the Redwood Console home. First thing is our usage overview. This is the top-level telemetry — tokens, requests, agg latency. But the interesting bit for you is the Endpoints tab — we call them routes in parts of the UI, but you can think of them as endpoints.
[01:05] [01:05] Darren O'Neil: Here I'm filtering to Cerulean's prod project. On the left are your endpoints — search-primary, summarize-stream, and conversation-annot. Clicking search-primary brings up per-minute traffic, p50/p95/p99 latency, and cost decomposition. The cost view breaks down compute token cost, KV cache hit savings, and infra allocation.
[01:27] Marcus Hale: That 'KV cache' bit — is that per-prefix? We sometimes see big reuse on repeated queries.
[01:33] Darren O'Neil: Yeah, we have prefix/KV caching breakdowns. The Console shows cache hit rate and estimated token savings — note that the estimator is sometimes conservative, it uses the last 24 hours by default.
[01:43] Lena Ortiz: Can we slice by model variant? We test an 8-bit quantized model and a float16; want to see cost delta.
[01:50] Darren O'Neil: Absolutely, model variant slicing is first-class here. You can stack the charts by variant or toggle to see cost per variant. Example: quantized-8bit shows ~40% token compute savings but slight latency bump at p99 in our example.
[02:05] Priya Kapoor: Does that include batching effects? Our traffic has bursts, batching can reduce cost but might increase tail latency.
[02:11] Darren O'Neil: Good point. The Console's cost model includes estimated batching efficiency based on observed concurrency and model throughput. We also surface expected latency impacts — there's a tradeoff slider you can simulate to see net unit cost at different batching windows.
[02:24] Maya Chen: One thing customers like is per-endpoint chargeback exports. Priya, you can export CSV for a date range with breakdown by endpoint, model, token class (prompt/response), and infra allocation.
[02:36] Priya Kapoor: Nice. For our billing system we need endpoint-level cost per day in UTC. CSV works. Does the export include user-defined tags?
[02:42] Darren O'Neil: Yes, tags and labels you set on each endpoint are included in the export.
[02:45] Marcus Hale: On infra allocation — for Dedicated pools can we pin endpoints to specific GPU pools for isolation?
[02:51] Darren O'Neil: Yep. Dedicated lets you reserve capacity and pin endpoints to capacity pools. The Console then attributes infra cost directly to those pinned endpoints; if an endpoint bursts and uses burst capacity, that shows as a separate line item.
[03:02] Lena Ortiz: Show us a canary/cutover example — we run A/B between a smaller quantized model and a larger one.
[03:07] Darren O'Neil: Sure. In rollout you can define canary traffic percentage and the Console shows per-variant metrics in real time — success rate, latency, cost delta. You can set automatic rollback rules (e.g., if error rate > 0.5% or p99 > 300ms).
[03:20] [03:20] Marcus Hale: Does Redwood provide pre-computed cost per token for different instance types? We want to compare GPU types for Dedicated.
[03:27] Darren O'Neil: The Console has a hardware cost model — you can select the pool type and it shows modeled per-token and per-request costs. It's configurable by your committed pricing as well so your accounting matches your contract.
[03:36] Lena Ortiz: Security/time to compliance — show audit logs and SSO.
[03:40] Darren O'Neil: Right, under Settings -> Security we keep audit trails of API key creation, route changes, and deployment events. SAML/SSO is in the tenant settings — we have out-of-the-box integrations with common IdPs. For encryption, customer-managed KMS keys can be used for model artifacts and logs.
[03:55] Priya Kapoor: Excellent. We also need retention controls and the ability to redact PII from request payloads before it's stored.
[04:02] Darren O'Neil: We offer configurable retention windows and a PII redaction pipeline you can enable at the route level. Note: redaction affects what we can show in raw trace logs — but telemetry aggregates remain.
[04:12] [04:12] Lena Ortiz: For our pilot we need to replicate a typical weekday traffic pattern — 100 RPS for search-primary at peak with 2k tokens avg. Can you run a benchmark?
[04:20] Maya Chen: Yes, Darren and I can run a throughput benchmark in our sandbox. Ideally you provide 48h traces so we can replay. Marcus, can you share traces?
[04:29] Marcus Hale: Yeah, I'll export traces. They have sensitive headers — we'll scrub PII first. We'll share an S3 link.
[04:34] Priya Kapoor: Timing? We want results before internal QBR on Aug 20.
[04:38] Maya Chen: We'll target running the bench week of Aug 10 and send results by Aug 14. We'll include latency/cost sensitivity across quantized vs float variants and Dedicated vs Hosted routing.
[04:47] [04:47] Marcus Hale: When you say Hosted vs Dedicated routing, what happens if a Dedicated pool is saturated? Do requests fail over to Hosted?
[04:54] Darren O'Neil: You can define fallback policies. Most customers configure soft fallbacks: route to a cheaper hosted variant or lower-cost model family. We also do circuit-breakers to avoid cascading failures. Fallbacks are visible in the Console as events with timestamps and reasons.
[05:06] Lena Ortiz: How precise is the cost attribution when fallback occurs? We need to charge teams for what they actually used.
[05:12] Darren O'Neil: We annotate each request with resolution metadata — which pool/variant served it, whether it used cached KV results, and any fallback. The export labels those so cost attribution is per served instance, not just configured routing.
[05:23] Priya Kapoor: Competitors sometimes only give you aggregate region-level costs — this per-request annotation is useful for us.
[05:29] Maya Chen: Quick demo of the per-request trace view — Darren, open the sample request.
[05:33] Darren O'Neil: (navigates) Here's a single request: timeline shows tokenization, KV lookup, model inference, post-processing. There's a note that KV hit saved ~300 tokens. There's also a small transcription error in the autogenerated note — 'K V cash' instead of 'KV cache' on rare cases because the speech engine mis-heard, sorry about that.
[05:50] Marcus Hale: Ha, noted.
[05:51] [05:51] Lena Ortiz: What about alerting for cost anomalies? We run experiments that can spike spend unexpectedly.
[05:56] Darren O'Neil: Console has anomaly detection: we baseline normal spend per-endpoint and send alerts via Slack/email when spend or tokens deviate by X sigma. You can create guardrails at route level to throttle or pause if spend hits a threshold.
[06:09] Priya Kapoor: For internal chargeback, we need a daily SKU-like report — endpoint, tokens, model, infra, and a computed internal price per token. Can the Console support a custom pricing function?
[06:17] Darren O'Neil: Yes, there's a custom pricing engine — you can set multipliers per pool, per model family, or apply overhead markup. Exports will reflect that.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Another useful feature is historical rolling windows — you can group by calendar month or 30-day sliding windows for smoothing.
[06:29] Marcus Hale: About latency: p99 matters to us. How well does the Console surface tail-latency breakdown across components?
[06:36] Darren O'Neil: It breaks down p99 into queueing, model inference, and network - from our observability hooks. For model inference we split warm vs cold starts; warm runs include KV hits and cached weights when available. For cold starts the Console shows the proportion of requests that incurred model load.
[06:50] Lena Ortiz: If we do on-prem Private deployment, do we still get the Console?
[06:55] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Private includes the Console control plane with options to host telemetry in your VPC and keep logs on-prem. There are subtle differences: in Private you manage the data retention and KMS fully; we ship a connector for dashboarding.
[07:08] Marcus Hale: For the pilot, we'd prefer Private but maybe start with Dedicated. Can you outline the migration path?
[07:14] Darren O'Neil: Migration is largely configuration-driven: pin endpoints to pools in Dedicated, then for Private you install the Private control plane, point agents at your infra, and migrate route configs. The Console keeps the same route IDs so historical metrics are preserved if you choose to backfill.
[07:27] [07:27] Priya Kapoor: Any notes on compliance? We need audit trail retention for 2 years and SOC2 Type II.
[07:33] Darren O'Neil: We maintain SOC2 Type II. Audit retention is configurable; for Private we can enable longer retention and integrate with your SIEM. We'll send the compliance pack.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Quick repricing example: here's an endpoint configured to use quantized-8 and fallback to hosted-base if Dedicated is saturated. You can see cost per 1,000 requests and estimated monthly spend.
[07:53] Marcus Hale: Sharing: we often proxy requests through our edge — does Redwood support client IP preservation for rate-limiting hooks?
[07:59] Darren O'Neil: Yes you can pass through X-Forwarded-For and we have rules for rate-limit enforcement in the Console.
[08:07] Lena Ortiz: Okay, timeline recap?
[08:10] Maya Chen: We committed: Darren will share SOC2 and SSO docs by Friday Aug 6, I'll send pricing and chargeback workbook by Sunday Aug 7, Marcus will share traces by Aug 12, and we'll run a benchmark week of Aug 10 and deliver results Aug 14 so you have them ahead of Aug 20 QBR.
[08:26] Priya Kapoor: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:29] Marcus Hale: One small ask — can you include per-endpoint memory footprint estimation in the bench? We care about instance sizing.
[08:35] Darren O'Neil: We'll include peak GPU memory and per-request memory delta in the bench report.
[08:40] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links to the shared folder and next steps.
[08:46] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[08:48] (meeting ends)
